text:
You know how Mrs. Gable used to have those big, round glasses that always slid down her nose? Well, guess what happened! I was just buying the sparkliest juice boxes ever at the Super-Mart when I saw her standing right by the cereal aisle. But she looked... different. Like, really different.

Her hair isn’t brown anymore; it’s like snow on a mountain top! And she wasn’t wearing her teacher clothes with the chalk dust. She had this fancy blue coat on and was holding a shopping basket instead of a ruler. At first, I didn’t even recognize her because she wasn’t yelling about quiet time or making us sit criss-cross applesauce.

Then, I waved my hand and said, "Hi, Mrs. Gable!" My voice came out squeaky because I was super nervous. She stopped looking at the corn flakes and squinted at me. Her eyes got all wide, like two shiny marbles. She gasped and dropped her basket! Okay, not literally, but it bounced really loud.

She said, "Is that you, Leo?" in this soft voice, way quieter than when she taught math. It was weird but cool. She remembered my name! After twenty whole years, which is basically forever for kids, she still knew who I was. We stood there talking about how fast time goes while people pushed carts around us. I felt so grown-up shaking her hand, but also kind of sad that school is over now.
